spec.title: ZAP: revising knowledge, value, and the achievable outcome

status.comment: The Owner clarification of 2026-09-12 is implemented through domain events and the persistent runtime; the coordinator confirms integration completeness against the complete denominator and stored evidence, without an additional approval ceremony.

p.INTENT-AND-HYPOTHESES: Intent states who needs the result and why. The current expected outcome is a testable hypothesis about how to realize that intent under known conditions. The plan is a hypothesis about the actions that lead to the chosen outcome. New knowledge may change both hypotheses; a new Owner instruction may also change the intent itself. The initial task list does not become an independent source of value.

p.ADMISSIBLE-OUTCOMES: Initial agreement defines the semantic space of admissible outcomes: required benefit, essential guarantees, preferences, and tradeoffs the agent may manage autonomously. The concrete outcome may change within that space, including after the original variant is proved impossible when a more valuable solution exists. The space need not enumerate every future variant; examples and counterexamples help assess new ones. Approximation is judged by preserved benefit and guarantees, not by similar names or the number of completed rows.

p.VALUE-AND-AUTHORITY: New information changes the expected contribution of capabilities to Owner values, their feasibility, and work priorities. Reassessment explicitly distinguishes changed knowledge about value from a change in the preference itself. The coordinator may change preferences or the tradeoff balance only within the delegated scope. It does not declare an essential condition optional because implementation is difficult. The charter may authorize choosing a nearby valuable outcome without a separate question at every turn.

p.FEEDBACK-LOOP: The cycle has observable steps: capture new signals; revise the knowledge model and fog of war; assess option value, cost, and feasibility; keep or revise the expected outcome and route; reconcile the work graph and live operations with the decision; perform the nearest valuable work; observe the result. It applies at campaign, workstream, and local-task levels. A confirmed local conclusion moves upward when it changes the basis of a higher outcome; a higher-level correction flows back into affected subwork.

p.REVIEW-TRIGGERS: Triggers include a material observation or contradiction, experiment result, changed external capability, material deviation in predicted cost or effect, new Owner instruction, newly valuable alternative, and reaching a boundary after which the result use scope changes. At natural integration points and before substantial investment, the basis is checked even without an explicit error. Expiration of an external observation creates a review basis when its currency matters; a timer is not portrayed as running without a runtime.

p.FOG-RECOMPUTATION: Fog of war need not decrease monotonically. A new fact may reveal an unknown region, split an old one into several questions, merge duplicate investigations, reopen a closed question, or change its relevance. When the expected outcome changes, the review checks which regions became relevant and which do not yet affect the chosen route. Loss of relevance is not acquired knowledge; absence of an explicit question does not prove that the world has been studied completely.

p.VALUE-REASSESSMENT: Options are compared by expected benefit to the intent, essential guarantees, remaining cost, time, risk, external dependencies, and reversibility. Qualitative assessments, ranges, and explicit unknown are allowed; precise numbers and weights require evidence. A universal score or model confidence percentage is not mandatory. Sunk cost does not justify continuation by itself; the actual value of preserved assets and switching cost are considered.

p.FEASIBILITY-AND-INFORMATION: Unknown feasibility differs from disproved feasibility, and impossibility of one method differs from impossibility of the outcome. A conclusion is bounded by captured conditions and the material alternatives tried. The next action may produce a result or information capable of changing the choice: a small experiment, research into an external constraint, or a check of an expensive assumption. Prefer research with a clear decision impact; studying the entire world is not a prerequisite for work.

p.REVIEW-OUTCOMES: A review may continue the current route with a preserved basis, reorder work, research, replace a method, revise the expected outcome, abandon work that lost value, wait for an actual capability, or prepare a concrete proposal outside delegated decisions. Outcome revision is allowed for a better opportunity, not only after failure. An unverified assessment is not presented as proof of impossibility.

p.BOUNDED-RECONSIDERATION: An ordinary cycle follows the links and assumptions affected by the signal. A campaign-goal review also checks link completeness and new regions outside the old graph: an incomplete graph does not prove absence of impact. A small change does not trigger complete replanning, rereading all history, or the full test panel. Without material new grounds the decision remains stable; priority oscillation requires an explanation of changed benefit and switching cost. Replanning must move valuable action closer rather than defer it indefinitely.

reconciliation.title: 3. Revising the plan without losing history

p.LOSSLESS-REVISION: Preserving obligations means no silent loss, not a ban on revising every original item. For the selected active outcome, an obligation receives implementation and verification. When outcome revision is authorized, every prior item receives an explicit disposition: retained, replaced with a named successor, excluded from accepted scope, or determined unattainable under named conditions. Rationale, authority, and the prior revision are preserved. Automatically adding subtasks does not replace this procedure and cannot cancel a requirement.

p.PLAN-RECONCILIATION: The new route reconciles obligations, tasks, dependencies, expected maturity, formal deferrals, evidence, priorities, and integration. Stale work may be replaced, removed from the current frontier, or returned for verification; missing work may be decomposed. Renaming does not create a new problem identity or reset stop counters. The history of abandoned methods remains, as does the distinction between cancelling a task and cancelling required benefit.

p.LIVE-WORK-RECONCILIATION: A review accounts for already dispatched tasks and unknown operation outcomes. Affected new runs use the new revision; running executors receive a concrete transition: finish a valuable compatible part, reach a safe boundary, or preserve a candidate for new verification. Editing a task record does not cancel the actual process. Unaffected authorized work continues unless a campaign-wide stop applies. A general Owner condition takes precedence over continuation during adaptation.

p.EVIDENCE-APPLICABILITY: An accepted historical result remains a fact of prior acceptance. A new outcome may require different guarantees, so the old result suitability for a new consumer is assessed separately. Acceptance status does not transfer proof to a changed subject. Applicable artifacts are reused, and repeated checks are selected according to the basis that actually changed.

p.REVISED-DEFERRALS: When the outcome changes, every deferral remains applicable, transfers to a successor, or receives a justified not-applicable disposition. An abandoned prototype need not undergo formal productization if it is truly no longer used; its external effects, preservation of required data, and permanent placement of unique knowledge are checked separately. Removing work from the interface or lowering priority does not prove that no consumers exist.

p.MEANINGFUL-COMPLETION: The result distinguishes achievement of the original outcome, achievement of an authorized revised outcome, partial benefit, and established unattainability under current conditions. Final verification compares the original intent, active outcome revision, and actual effect. Readiness does not increase by deleting difficult tasks or shrinking the denominator. If valuable continuation requires leaving the mandate, the coordinator prepares a concrete choice; already authorized work continues within its conditions. It must not promise continuous execution when no valuable authorized action remains or rename that impossibility as success.

observability.title: 4. What is stored and what is computed

p.REVIEW-RECORD: A material review links its trigger, source intent and plan revisions, captured facts, prior and new uncertainty assessment, alternatives with value and feasibility assessments, decision, and authority basis. It lists outcome and obligation changes, affected tasks and evidence, actions for live jobs, and the next review trigger. Keeping the existing plan may itself be a substantive review result. Routine unchanged observations need no separate literary report.

p.MODEL-AND-KERNEL: The agent identifies semantic relationships, assesses value, forms alternatives, and explains the choice. Algorithms compute known dependency closure, validate references, allowed transitions, complete explicit dispositions, expected revisions, and stop rules; they build projections and a change journal. A changed knowledge model may require new links an old algorithmic traversal cannot find. The viewer displays stored assessments and uncertainty; replay does not perform a new semantic reassessment.

p.ATOMIC-REVIEW: An adaptive transition publishes a coherent current revision of the outcome, graph, and dispositions while checking captured versions. A stale assessment rereads changed inputs before acceptance. The journal explains why changed knowledge produced a different priority or outcome. Proposed and accepted revisions and actual application to executors remain distinct; neither a JSON file nor an updated graph proves that an external action occurred.

p.PROTOTYPE-BOUNDARY: The adaptive transition is implemented with separate proposed/applied states. It binds intent/outcome, obligation dispositions, ownership, work changes, source and knowledge captures, and live-job reconciliation. Policy and CAS are checked at application; the runtime performs job effects separately. The command contract and capabilities publish the actual operation set.

p.CASE-NEW-FOG: Research into an external package discovers an installation method and an unexamined background service. The old question gains evidence, a new unknown region appears, and integration cost changes. If the service is irrelevant to the chosen scenario, it is marked currently irrelevant; this does not prove the service is absent or authorize leaving the original scope.

p.CASE-REVISED-OUTCOME: The Owner wants to automate a repeatable service setup as far as possible and permits one manual step in advance as a valuable approximation. Research shows that a particular operation has no API. The coordinator compares available alternatives and may select automation of the remaining procedure with the manual step stated explicitly. The final report shows the revised outcome and remaining constraint. If full automation made manual steps an essential prohibition, this proposal is not an authorized substitute without corresponding authority.

p.CASE-BETTER-OPPORTUNITY: After a successful prototype, an available component is found that delivers the required benefit at lower remaining cost. A working custom prototype does not require continuing the old route. Once suitability is established, the route and nearest work change, reusable checks and knowledge are preserved, and switching cost is explicit.

p.CASE-NO-SELF-SUCCESS: An executor encounters a difficult check and proposes removing the essential property it protects to obtain a green status. That substitution has no basis in the authorized outcome and is rejected. Disproving the original method may lead to research or an admissible approximation, but changing the criterion or renaming the problem cannot bypass the charter or stop conditions.

p.CASE-STOP-SURVIVES-PIVOT: After two architectural approaches to one problem fail, renaming the current goal or choosing an approximate outcome does not clear the confirmed campaign-wide stop. Problem history remains. Available alternatives may be prepared for the Owner, but a third attempt is not launched under the name of adaptation.
